title: UnicodeEncodeError when indexing PDFs with surrogate characters in extracted text
body:
## Description

PaperQA2 crashes with `UnicodeEncodeError` when indexing certain PDFs that contain mathematical symbols which extract as invalid Unicode surrogate characters.

## Error

```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\udc63' in position 9603: surrogates not allowed
```

Full traceback:
```
File "/home/matthias/.pyenv/versions/sys/lib/python3.12/site-packages/paperqa/agents/search.py", line 298, in _add_document
    body_filehash = self.filehash(index_doc["body"])
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
File "/home/matthias/.pyenv/versions/sys/lib/python3.12/site-packages/paperqa/agents/search.py", line 261, in filehash
    return hexdigest(body)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
File "/home/matthias/.pyenv/versions/sys/lib/python3.12/site-packages/paperqa/utils.py", line 103, in hexdigest
    data = data.encode("utf-8")
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\udc63' in position 9603: surrogates not allowed
```

## Root Cause

Some PDFs (especially those with mathematical notation) use custom fonts with character mappings that pypdf cannot translate to valid Unicode. The extracted text contains orphaned UTF-16 surrogate characters (e.g., `\udc63`, `\udc65`, `\udc66`) which are invalid in UTF-8.

Example from affected PDF (arXiv:1711.07566 "Neural 3D Mesh Renderer"):
```python
# Page 2 extracted text contains:
'\udc63" = (\udc65", \udc66")\n\udc43*\t, \udc3c*(\udc65")'
# These should be mathematical italic characters (𝑐, 𝑥, 𝑦, 𝑃, 𝐼)
```

## Suggested Fix

In `paperqa/utils.py`, the `hexdigest` function should sanitize the text before encoding:

```python
def hexdigest(data: str | bytes) -> str:
    if isinstance(data, str):
        # Replace invalid surrogates with replacement character
        data = data.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogateescape").decode("utf-8", errors="replace").encode("utf-8")
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
```

Or more simply:
```python
def hexdigest(data: str | bytes) -> str:
    if isinstance(data, str):
        data = data.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
```

## Environment

- paper-qa version: latest from pip
- Python: 3.12
- OS: Linux

## Reproduction

1. Download PDF from https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.07566
2. Run `pqa ask "test query"` with that PDF in the index directory
3. Crash occurs during indexing

<!-- Greeting -->
Hi @hummat! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the paper-qa team.

<!-- Answer -->
The crash happens because extracted PDF text can contain invalid Unicode surrogate characters, which Python can't encode to UTF-8. The current hexdigest implementation in paperqa/utils.py doesn't handle these, so when the extracted text is hashed for indexing, it raises a UnicodeEncodeError [code reference](https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa/blob/8221e3cf8b7ff7b2485cd9e05e44387dab183a0a/paperqa/utils.py#L98-L101).

Your suggested fix—encoding with errors="replace" in hexdigest—is safe and effective. It replaces invalid surrogates with the Unicode replacement character (�), preventing the crash without affecting the hash-based deduplication logic elsewhere in the code [code reference](https://github.com/Future-House/paper-qa/blob/8221e3cf8b7ff7b2485cd9e05e44387dab183a0a/paperqa/agents/search.py#L275-L345). There’s no evidence of unintended side effects, since all downstream consumers of the hash expect a bytes digest, not the original text.

Recommended change:

```python
def hexdigest(data: str | bytes) -> str:
    if isinstance(data, str):
        data = data.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    return hashlib.md5(data).hexdigest()
```

This will make indexing robust to malformed Unicode in extracted PDF text. If you want to be even more defensive, consider applying similar sanitization at other text ingestion points, but fixing hexdigest is sufficient to resolve this crash.
